_: AD-22. The Impact page's own editorial content. THE FIGURES ARE NOT HERE ON PURPOSE — every number on the page is read out of data/work/**, so /impact cannot disagree with the item page it came from. That was the defect class that had the situation index showing 412 while the Air page said 387. Anything in this file that names a figure names it by (kind, slug, label) and the build resolves it; a reference that does not resolve is a build failure, not a blank.

frame._: Chosen on measurement. 2400x1600 and TRULY landscape (EXIF orientation 1), with the highest RMS contrast of any frame in the library at 92 — and contrast, not brightness, is what lets a subject read through the halftone screen. The crop is 80%, chosen by rendering six candidate strips and looking at them rather than by the contrast metric alone: the metric preferred 19%, which fills the band with the placard's own lettering and puts CLEAN AIR IS OUR RIGHT in direct typographic competition with the headline. At 80% the placard is reduced to a bright edge and the band is a row of faces — people, countable, which is what this page is about. The two frames tried before it, trekkers-hillside and snow-trek-group, both carry EXIF orientation 6: they are 1500x2000 PORTRAIT as a browser lays them out, and putting a portrait photograph in a 1440x360 letterbox showed a thin horizontal sliver of a tall image. That, and not tonality, is what "the image is not visible" was. The subject also earns its place: students with hand-lettered placards is people, countable, and the nearest thing in our archive to the policy claim this page is still waiting on.

masthead.lead: The figures are not added together, because the people they count are the same people.

refuse.head:
Why there is
no total
refuse.lead: The figures below count overlapping groups of people over periods that do not line up. Added together they would be a larger number and a false one.
refuse.overlap_intro: One young person can be inside all four at once:

overlap.label: Girls and boys through the programme

argument.h: The populations overlap, and nothing records by how much
argument.p: A volunteer who walked an eco-walk is counted in the first two. A girl who came through ME to WE and then led a Yatra is in the last two. Nobody has ever recorded which person is in which programme.

argument.h: The periods do not share a denominator
argument.p: One of those four is annual, one is two decades, one is since 2004 and one is thirteen years. A sum over four different spans is not a quantity. It is four quantities printed next to each other with a plus sign between them.

refuse.rule: An organisation that declines to average micrograms and milligrams does not get to add up children.

pair.head:
Two numbers,
one programme
pair.lead: Bridge the Gap publishes two figures that a reader will assume are rival versions of the same count. They are not. They are answers to two different questions, and the difference between them is the point.

rows.h: One counts reach. The other counts effect.
rows.p: The larger figure counts children in a school the programme entered. The smaller counts children who sat the sessions. Reach is what an organisation can claim; effect is what it can be held to. Both belong on the page, labelled, because publishing only the first is advertising and publishing only the second hides the scale of the work.

rows.h: One is counted. The other is derived.
rows.p: The smaller figure is a count of real schools and real students. The larger is arithmetic — schools a year, times years, times the children in a school — and the middle term of that is an estimate.

sheet._: CELL ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Cells 1 and 8 span two columns at 8:3, so both must hold a genuinely wide frame — the first build put clean-air-protest (1.50) and community-meal (0.75, portrait) in them and cropped both to slivers. Positions 1 and 8 are now 2.17 and 2.45. Every other cell is 4:3, where a portrait frame crops honestly. Gated in the generator against the library, which is itself now checked against the files.

act._: AD-39, owner instruction 24 August: REMOVE THE 'HOLD US TO IT' SECTION AND PUT TABS HERE -- About us, Get involved, Work. What was here was a band called 'Hold us to it' whose lead read 'A register is only worth the checking' and whose three bordered door cards pointed at /work, /act and /now. Two things were wrong with it. The head was an instruction to the reader about how to treat our own page, which is the category AD-28 spent a whole review removing; and three bordered boxes are the only bordered boxes on this page, so the band read as a different design language arriving at the end. The tabs are the device the rest of the site already uses for a set of destinations -- the same component as the register above it on this very page. THE THREE ARE THE OWNER'S THREE, in his order. /now is not among them and that is his call, not an omission this file should quietly repair: it is a nav word on every page and it now has six rows of its own in the footer. NOTHING IS LOST FROM THE OLD BAND: the 'Give us a number' invitation, which was the only content in it that this page uniquely needed, is the second sentence of the Get involved panel.
